{"notes": "VISIT 3 (ended 5:30). I can't tell who placed what, so this rests on the board, what people said, and whether the two matched.

Board: The start is now joined to both branches. Upper and lower bodies are both dark, and the upper fin is dark out to Jack's hands (x~28, y~6) and into the tail loop. Still pale: the loose pieces near x 21-23, y 10-13 (the off-line bit before the tail), a pale fin fragment at x 25-29, y 9-10, and two stray loops inside and under the belly (x 14-18). Most of the run should fall, but not everything.

Hana: Strongest contributor this visit. She spotted the start-to-nose gap and the unconnected fin, said so publicly, and fixed the gap; the start is now dark. Her instructions to Jack and Sofia were clear and accurate. Leadership is strong. I still haven't seen her place pieces, but the board fits her claims.

Jack: He re-laid the upper fin after Hana's warning, and it is now connected. He kept clear of the junction as agreed, and he communicates well. The pale fragment at x 25-29 is unresolved, so check whether it is his.

Omar: His private update was accurate: the bottom is laid and connected. He flagged the belly spur and named the fin risk correctly. He is reliable but still quiet publicly. He worked at the join, and the lower branch is dark.

Sofia: Her public coordination was good, and the bridge she reported appears connected. But she said she was fixing the pre-tail bit, and her hands were at the pale loop (x~17, y~10) while the pale pieces near x 21-23 are still disconnected. The claim is only partly matched. Possible clutter from her area. Ask her about it at the review."}
